citation: Tiekou Lorinczova H, Deb S, Begum G et al. (2021). Comparative Assessment of the Acute Effects of Whey, Rice and Potato Protein Isolate Intake on Markers of Glycaemic Regulation and Appetite in Healthy Males Using a Randomised Study Design. Nutrients 13(7):2157.
protocol: Three isocaloric shakes (~233 kcal), randomised crossover: ~45.5 g whey protein isolate vs rice protein vs potato protein, each in orange juice (~7-10 g carbohydrate). Blood at 0, 30, 60, 120, 180 min.
population: n=9 healthy men, age 30.8 ± 9.3 y, body weight 86.6 ± 6.7 kg (21-47 y).

reports.where: Table 3: total iAUC per protein (mean ± SD)
Results text: differences between proteins at 30 min

note: Paired-meal contrast, protein_source: whey vs rice vs potato protein drinks at matched protein and energy. Animal vs two plant isolates at a large protein dose with almost no carbohydrate, good for protein-driven insulin. Watch: carbohydrate from juice differs a little (7.1-9.8 g), only areas are tabulated and their units need checking. Only in figures: glucose, insulin and GLP-1 time courses.
